blocks.content: A Persistent Volume is a piece of storage provisioned at the cluster level, existing entirely independently of any specific Pod's lifecycle, exactly the durability the ordinary Volumes covered in the previous topic do not provide.

Unlike the Pod-scoped Volumes from the previous topic, a PV is its own, independent object in the cluster, it does not belong to any particular Pod, Deployment, or namespace, it simply exists as a unit of available storage.

blocks.alt: An independent resource, not scoped to any particular Pod

metadata:
  name: pv-data
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 10Gi
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  hostPath:
    path: /data/pv-data

blocks.content: 2. Its Lifecycle Is Independent of Any Pod
blocks.text: 2. Its Lifecycle Is Independent of Any Pod

blocks.content: This is the entire point: a PV keeps existing regardless of how many Pods come and go, or are replaced, exactly the durability property covered in the Pod Replacement topic pointed toward needing.

blocks.alt: Outliving any individual Pod that ever used it

blocks.content: A PV is not an abstract placeholder, it maps to actual physical or cloud storage, an AWS EBS volume, a GCP persistent disk, an NFS share, whatever the underlying infrastructure actually is.

blocks.alt: A real mapping to actual, physical or cloud-provisioned storage

blocks.content: Unlike most objects covered so far, a PV is not namespaced (namespaces are covered fully in their own module), it exists at the whole-cluster level, available to be claimed from any namespace.

blocks.alt: Existing above the namespace level entirely

blocks.content: 5. How a PV Actually Gets Created
blocks.text: 5. How a PV Actually Gets Created

blocks.content: A PV can be created manually by a cluster administrator ahead of time (static provisioning), or created automatically on demand, covered fully in the Dynamic Provisioning topic later in this module.

blocks.alt: Created by hand, or automatically, covered in full later in this module

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: A Persistent Volume is a cluster-scoped storage resource that exists independently of any specific Pod, mapping to real, underlying physical or cloud storage.
It can be created manually ahead of time by an administrator, or automatically on demand, the mechanism covered in the Dynamic Provisioning topic.
